Updating ose-baremetal-runtimecfg-container image to be consistent with ART for 4.22
__TLDR__:
Product builds by ART can be configured for different base and builder images than corresponding CI
builds. This automated PR requests a change to CI configuration to align with ART's configuration;
please take steps to merge it quickly or contact ART to coordinate changes.

The configuration in the following ART component metadata is driving this alignment request:
[baremetal-runtimecfg.yml](https://github.com/openshift/ocp-build-data/tree/532305ad2d84f57355ac03b308650bcc5a8d7740/images/baremetal-runtimecfg.yml).

__Detail__:

This repository is out of sync with the downstream product builds for this component. The CI
configuration for at least one image differs from ART's expected product configuration. This should
be addressed to ensure that the component's CI testing accurate reflects what customers will
experience.

Most of these PRs are opened as an ART-driven proposal to migrate base image or builder(s) to a
different version, usually prior to GA. The intent is to effect changes in both configurations
simultaneously without breaking either CI or ART builds, so usually ART builds are configured to
consider CI as canonical and attempt to match CI config until the PR merges to align both. ART may
also configure changes in GA releases with CI remaining canonical for a brief grace period to enable
CI to succeed and the alignment PR to merge. In either case, ART configuration will be made
canonical at some point (typically at branch-cut before GA or release dev-cut after GA), so it is
important to align CI configuration as soon as possible.

PRs are also triggered when CI configuration changes without ART coordination, for instance to
change the number of builder images or to use a different golang version. These changes should be
coordinated with ART; whether ART configuration is canonical or not, preferably it would be updated
first to enable the changes to occur simultaneously in both CI and ART at the same time. This also
gives ART a chance to validate the intended changes first. For instance, ART compiles most
components with the Golang version being used by the control plane for a given OpenShift release.
Exceptions to this convention (i.e. you believe your component must be compiled with a Golang
version independent from the control plane) must be granted by the OpenShift staff engineers and
communicated to the ART team.

__Roles & Responsibilities__:
- Component owners are responsible for ensuring these alignment PRs merge with passing
  tests OR that necessary metadata changes are reported to the ART team: `@release-artists`
  in `#forum-ocp-art` on Slack. If necessary, the changes required by this pull request can be
  introduced with a separate PR opened by the component team. Once the repository is aligned,
  this PR will be closed automatically.
- In particular, it could be that a job like `verify-deps` is complaining. In that case, please open
  a new PR with the dependency issues addressed (and base images bumped). [ART-9595](https://issues.redhat.com//browse/ART-9595) for reference.
- Patch-manager or those with sufficient privileges within this repository may add
  any required labels to ensure the PR merges once tests are passing. In cases where ART config is
  canonical, downstream builds are *already* being built with these changes, and merging this PR
  only improves the fidelity of our CI. In cases where ART config is not canonical, this provides
  a grace period for the component team to align their CI with ART's configuration before it becomes
  canonical in product builds.

ART has been configured to reconcile your CI build root image (see https://docs.ci.openshift.org/docs/architecture/ci-operator/#build-root-image).
In order for your upstream .ci-operator.yaml configuration to be honored, you must set the following in your openshift/release ci-operator configuration file:
```
build_root:
  from_repository: true
```

__Change behavior of future PRs__:
* In case you just want to follow the base images that ART suggests, you can configure additional labels to be
  set up automatically. This means that such a PR would *merge without human intervention* (and awareness!) in the future.
  To do so, open a PR to set the `auto_label` attribute in the image configuration. [Example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/pull/1778)
* You can set a commit prefix, like `UPSTREAM: <carry>: `. [An example](https://github.com/openshift-eng/ocp-build-data/blob/6831b59dddc5b63282076d3abe04593ad1945148/images/ose-cluster-api.yml#L11).

If you have any questions about this pull request, please reach out to `@release-artists` in the `#forum-ocp-art` coreos slack channel.

author: slauger
body:
## Summary

This PR modernizes the `github_actions_runner` module with significant enhancements for security, flexibility, and adherence to modern Puppet best practices. The main improvements include:

- **Runner registration token support** - Use repository runner registration tokens instead of PATs
- **Runner self-updates** - Allow runners to update themselves without re-registration
- **Proxy support** - Full proxy configuration for API calls and downloads
- **User management** - Create and manage dedicated non-root runner users
- **Hiera-based configuration** - All defaults moved to data layer with architecture-specific hierarchy
- **Vagrant testing infrastructure** - Complete local testing environment
- **Runner deregistration** - Automatic cleanup when removing runners
- **Modern Puppet syntax** - Updated to current best practices
- **Puppet-lint compliance** - All linter warnings resolved
- **Restructured tests** - Split monolithic specs into 7 focused, feature-organized files

## Key Features

### 1. Runner Registration Token Support (`repo_token`)

Instead of requiring a Personal Access Token (PAT) with broad permissions (`admin:org`, `repo`), users can now provide runner registration tokens directly from repository settings.

**Benefits:**
- More secure: No need for PATs with admin permissions
- Better for repository-level runners
- Clear separation between PAT-based and token-based workflows

**Configuration:**
```yaml
github_actions_runner::instances:
  example_repo_instance:
    repo_name: 'myrepo'
    repo_token: 'AAAAABBBBBCCCCCDDDDD'  # Runner registration token
    labels:
      - self-hosted-custom
```

### 2. Runner Self-Updates (`version_in_path`)

New parameter `version_in_path` (default: `true` for backwards compatibility) controls installation path structure.

**When `version_in_path: false`:**
- Installation path: `/opt/actions-runner/` (no version suffix)
- Runners can self-update without Puppet re-registration
- `_work/` directory preserved across updates
- Recommended when using runner registration tokens

**Configuration:**
```yaml
github_actions_runner::version_in_path: false
github_actions_runner::disable_update: false  # Allow self-updates
```

### 3. Vagrant Testing Infrastructure

Complete local testing environment with cross-platform support:

**Features:**
- Support for VMware Fusion 13+, Parallels, and VirtualBox
- Hiera-based configuration for easy testing
- Automatic module syncing via Vagrant shared folders
- Complete test environment with Puppet 8 and required modules
- Detailed documentation in `examples/README.md`

**Quick Start:**
```bash
cd examples/
vagrant up
vagrant ssh
```

### 4. Runner Deregistration

Automatic cleanup when removing runners:

- Cleanly removes runners from GitHub before deleting files
- Uses GitHub's native `config.sh remove --token` command
- Prevents orphaned runners in GitHub settings
- Triggered automatically when setting `ensure: absent`

**Configuration:**
```yaml
github_actions_runner::instances:
  old_runner:
    ensure: absent  # Runner will be deregistered and removed
```

### 5. Proxy Support

Full proxy support for API calls (PAT-based authentication) and package downloads.

**Configuration:**
```yaml
github_actions_runner::http_proxy: http://proxy.local
github_actions_runner::https_proxy: http://proxy.local
github_actions_runner::no_proxy: localhost,example.com
```

### 6. User Management

Create dedicated non-root users for running runners securely.

**Configuration:**
```yaml
github_actions_runner::users:
  github-runner:
    home: /home/github-runner
    shell: /bin/bash
  prod-runner:
    home: /srv/prod-runner
    groups:
      - docker

github_actions_runner::instances:
  standard_runner:
    repo_name: 'public-repo'
    user: github-runner
    repo_token: 'TOKEN1'
```

### 7. Hiera-Based Configuration

All defaults moved to Hiera data layer with architecture-specific hierarchy.

**Structure:**
```
data/
├── common.yaml              # Default values
└── os/
    ├── x86_64.yaml         # Intel/AMD 64-bit
    ├── amd64.yaml          # Intel/AMD 64-bit (alternative name)
    └── aarch64.yaml        # ARM 64-bit
```

## Technical Improvements

### Modern Puppet Syntax
- Use `$key in $hash` instead of deprecated `has_key()`
- Use EPP templates (`.epp`) exclusively
- Use Hiera 5 with data-in-modules pattern
- Use `stdlib::deferrable_epp()` for deferred evaluation
- Iterator-based instance creation (`.each`) instead of `create_resources`

### Puppet-lint Compliance
- Fixed all parameter_types warnings by adding explicit type declarations
- Fixed selector_inside_resource warning by extracting selector logic
- Fixed params_not_optional_with_undef warnings using Optional types
- All validation checks pass

### RuboCop Compliance
- Fixed Layout/DotPosition errors (dots at end of line in method chains)
- Fixed Style/RegexpLiteral violations
- Fixed Style/TrailingCommaInArguments in hash definitions
- All style checks pass

### Test Improvements

Restructured from 2 monolithic files (1377 lines) to 7 focused files (890 lines):

**Class Tests:**
- `spec/classes/class_basic_spec.rb` - Root directory, instances, validation
- `spec/classes/class_users_spec.rb` - User and group management

**Define Tests:**
- `spec/defines/instance_basic_spec.rb` - Directory, archive, systemd, ownership
- `spec/defines/instance_tokens_spec.rb` - PAT auth, runner registration tokens, org/enterprise runners
- `spec/defines/instance_proxy_spec.rb` - Proxy configuration, archive proxy, systemd proxy
- `spec/defines/instance_paths_spec.rb` - .path and .env file management

**Shared Context:**
- `spec/support/spec/shared_contexts.rb` - Centralized version management

## Files Changed

### Core Files
- **README.md** - Comprehensive documentation for all new features
- **REFERENCE.md** - Updated parameter documentation (auto-generated)

### Data Layer
- **data/common.yaml** - Default values for all parameters
- **data/os/{x86_64,amd64,aarch64}.yaml** - Architecture-specific package names
- **hiera.yaml** - Hiera 5 configuration with architecture hierarchy

### Testing Infrastructure
- **examples/** - Complete Vagrant-based testing environment
- **examples/README.md** - Detailed testing documentation
- **examples/Vagrantfile** - Cross-platform VM configuration
- **examples/vagrant_files/** - Hiera configuration for testing

### Manifests
- **manifests/init.pp** - User management, Hiera-based defaults
- **manifests/instance.pp** - Token logic, proxy support, deregistration

### Templates
- **templates/configure_install_runner.sh.epp** - Runner configuration script
- **templates/github-actions-runner.service.epp** - Systemd service with proxy support
- **templates/path.epp** - PATH configuration
- **templates/env.epp** - Environment variables

### Tests
- **spec/classes/** - 2 files for main class testing
- **spec/defines/** - 4 files for instance define testing
- **spec/support/spec/shared_contexts.rb** - Shared test configuration

## Breaking Changes

**None.** All changes are backwards compatible:
- `version_in_path` defaults to `true` (existing behavior)
- PAT-based authentication still works
- All existing parameters retain their functionality

## Example Configuration

body:
## 📋 요약

레거시 로컬 업로드 URL 및 URL/키 혼재로 인해  
프로필 팝오버, 프로필 꾸미기, 문제 이미지가 깨지던 케이스를 해결했습니다.

백엔드/프론트 양쪽에 **정규화 + fallback 보정 로직**을 추가하여  
DB 마이그레이션 전·후, 그리고 레거시 데이터가 섞여 있어도  
항상 **일관된 키 기반 처리 + 안정적인 이미지 렌더링**이 가능하도록 개선했습니다.

또한 S3 URL 직렬화 범위를 **프로필 이미지로만 한정**하고  
테마/아바타/팝오버 꾸미기 값은 **키 그대로 주고받도록 구조를 정리**했습니다.

---

## 🛠 주요 변경 사항

### Backend

#### UserMapper / DTO 정합성 개선
- `UserMapper.xml`의 `UserPopoverMap`을 DTO 필드와 정확히 매핑
  - `id`, `profileTheme`, `avatarDecoration`, `popoverDecoration`, `following`
- `UserPopoverResponse`의 식별자 필드를 `id`로 통일

#### S3 직렬화 범위 조정
- **프로필 이미지(profileImage)만 S3 URL 직렬화 적용**
- 테마 / 아바타 / 팝오버 꾸미기 값은 **S3 직렬화 제거**
- DB ↔ API ↔ Front 간 **키 그대로 전달**

#### UserServiceImpl 정규화 로직 추가
- 프로필 업데이트 시  
  - 테마/아바타/팝오버 값이 URL로 넘어오면  
    → **파일명(확장자 제외) 기준으로 키로 정규화하여 저장**
- `getUserProfile`, `getUserPopover` 응답도  
  - 동일한 정규화 로직을 거쳐 반환  
  - → 프론트 매칭 안정성 확보

#### 레거시 URL 보정 (Fallback)
- `S3UrlSerializer`에서 레거시 업로드 URL 보정 처리
- DB 마이그레이션 전/후 모두 안전하게 동작

---

### Frontend

#### UserPopoverCard fallback 보강
- 데코레이션 키를 찾지 못하는 경우  
  - **값 자체를 이미지 URL로 취급하는 fallback 추가**
- 백엔드에서 URL이 넘어오는 경우에도  
  - 팝오버 배경/데코가 비지 않도록 방어 처리

#### resolveImageUrl와 연계된 이중 안전장치
- 백엔드/프론트 중 한쪽만 보정돼도  
  - 화면이 깨지지 않도록 설계

---

## 💡 핵심 기술 및 의사결정

### 1. 문제 원인 (Root Cause)
- 과거 데이터에는 다음 값들이 혼재
  - 로컬 업로드 URL
  - S3 URL
  - S3 Key
- 특히 **꾸미기/테마 계열 값이 URL로 저장된 경우**
  - 프론트의 키 기반 매핑이 실패하면서
  - 팝오버/프로필 UI가 깨지는 문제 발생

---

### 2. 해결 전략: “키 기반 일관성 + Fallback”
#### 즉시 DB 마이그레이션만 하지 않은 이유
- 운영 DB / 팀원 로컬 DB에 레거시 데이터가 섞여 있음
- 환경별 데이터 차이로 동일 이슈 재발 가능성 존재

#### 선택한 접근
- DB 저장 시점 + 응답 시점 + 프론트 렌더링 시점  
  → 모든 단계에서 **정규화 + fallback**
- 어떤 형태(URL / Key)로 데이터가 오더라도  
  → 최종 UI는 항상 정상 렌더링

---

### 3. S3 직렬화 정책 재정의
- **이미지 리소스**
  - `profileImage` → S3 URL 직렬화 유지
- **논리 값**
  - `theme` / `avatar` / `popover` → 키 그대로 유지
- 역할 분리로 책임 명확화
  - “URL은 이미지에만”
  - “상태 값은 키로만”

---

## 📸 Test & Verification
- 서버 재기동 후
  - `/users/{id}/popover`
  - 댓글 팝오버
  - 퀴즈 / 문제 조회  
  → 모두 정상 동작 확인 ✅
- 기존 DB에 URL이 섞여 있는 상태에서도  
  - 키 또는 URL이 정상 매칭되어 렌더링됨을 로그 기준으로 확인 ✅
- 신규 데이터 / 레거시 데이터 혼합 상황 모두 검증 완료 ✅

---

## ☑️ To-Do / Next Steps
- **DB 정리 (선택)**
  - 레거시 URL을 일괄 S3 Key로 마이그레이션해 데이터 일관성 강화
- **CloudFront 도입 시**
  - `spring.cloud.aws.s3.url`을 CDN 도메인으로 교체
  - 추가 코드 변경 없이 즉시 적용 가능

## Summary

Fix the publish workflow to work with the monorepo structure.

### Problem

The publish workflow was running `npm publish` from the root directory, but:
- Root `package.json` has `"private": true` so it would fail
- The actual publishable SDK is in `sdk/`

### Solution

Set `working-directory: sdk` for all npm commands so that:
- `npm ci` installs sdk dependencies
- `npm run build` builds the sdk
- `npm test` runs sdk tests
- `npm publish` publishes the sdk package

- [ ] Merge this PR first
- [ ] Then create GitHub release for v0.10.0
- [ ] Verify npm publish workflow succeeds

body:
## Summary

This PR adds the ability to search dictionary items by their **translation values** in addition to **keys**.  
The feature is **opt-in via configuration** and is **disabled by default** to preserve backward compatibility and performance.

---

## Changes

### 1. New Configuration Setting

- Created `DictionarySettings.cs`
  - New configuration class for dictionary-specific settings
- Added `EnableValueSearch` property
  - Boolean flag to enable value searching
  - Default: `false`
- Registered in `Constants-Configuration.cs`
  - Added `ConfigDictionary` constant
- Registered in DI container
  - Added to `UmbracoBuilder.Configuration.cs`

---

### 2. Repository Updates

- Modified `DictionaryRepository.cs`
  - Injected `IOptions<DictionarySettings>` into constructor
  - Updated `GetDictionaryItemDescendants` to support value search when enabled
- Search behavior:
  - When enabled, SQL queries search:
    - `cmsDictionary.key` using `LIKE 'filter%'`
    - `cmsLanguageText.value` using `LIKE '%filter%'`
  - When disabled, original behavior is preserved (key search only)

---

### 3. Test Updates

- Updated `DictionaryRepositoryTest.cs`
  - Added `DictionarySettings` parameter to test setup

---

## Configuration

To enable dictionary value search, add the following to your `appsettings.json`:

    {
      "Umbraco": {
        "CMS": {
          "Dictionary": {
            "EnableValueSearch": true
          }
        }
      }
    }

---

## Search Behavior

### When `EnableValueSearch == false` (Default)

- Searches only in dictionary keys
- Uses `key LIKE 'searchterm%'` (starts with)
- Maintains existing performance characteristics

### When `EnableValueSearch == true`

- Searches in both dictionary keys and translation values
- Uses:
  - `key LIKE 'searchterm%'`
  - `value LIKE '%searchterm%'`
- Key search uses **starts with**
- Value search uses **contains**

---

## Performance Testing

**Tested with:**

- 1,000 dictionary items
- 8 active languages:
  - `en-US`, `sq`, `da-DK`, `nb-NO`, `sv-SE`, `de-DE`, `fr-FR`, `es-ES`
- 8,000 total translations

**Results:**

- Average response time: **20–30 ms**
- Search scope: **All descendants with filter applied**
- Database: **SQL Server LocalDB**
- Performance is acceptable for typical dictionary sizes in production environments

Umbraco Docs link: https://github.com/umbraco/UmbracoDocs/pull/7734

## Summary

Implements support for OpenVPN's `--peer-fingerprint` option, enabling PKI-less authentication using SHA256 certificate fingerprints instead of a CA chain.

Closes #1361

## Changes

- Add `--auth-mode` option (`pki` or `fingerprint`) for install command
- Use Easy-RSA's `self-sign-server` and `self-sign-client` commands for fingerprint mode
- Server stores client fingerprints in `<peer-fingerprint>` block in `server.conf`
- Clients verify server using `peer-fingerprint` directive instead of CA
- Revocation removes fingerprint from config and reloads OpenVPN (instant effect)
- Version check ensures OpenVPN 2.6+ when fingerprint mode is selected

## Usage

```bash
# Interactive mode prompts for auth mode choice

# CLI mode
./openvpn-install.sh install --auth-mode fingerprint
```

## Comparison

| Aspect | PKI Mode | Fingerprint Mode |
|--------|----------|------------------|
| Server cert | CA-signed | Self-signed |
| Client cert | CA-signed | Self-signed |
| Revocation | CRL-based | Remove fingerprint |
| OpenVPN | Any version | 2.6.0+ required |
| Best for | Large deployments | Small/home setups |
